title: As a developer, files move through a real API — upload, download, list, move, and delete over documented REST endpoints, not just a desktop client
As a developer, big files upload reliably — documented chunked/resumable upload sessions that survive a dropped connection
As a developer, version history is addressable — file revisions can be listed and restored via the API, with documented retention windows
As a developer, I can sync efficiently — a cursor/delta endpoint returns only what changed since my last call instead of forcing a full re-crawl
As a developer, file events push to me — documented webhooks/change notifications fire when content changes, with verification and retry semantics spelled out
As a power user, sync just works on my machines — official desktop clients across macOS/Windows with selective sync and on-demand (online-only) files
As a developer, sharing is programmable — shared links with visibility, password, and expiry settings can be created and revoked via the API
As an IT admin, permissions are granular — folder- and file-level roles (viewer/commenter/editor/owner) with inheritance behavior documented
As an IT admin, external collaboration is governed — org-level controls over who can share outside the team, with domain allowlists or link restrictions
As a founder, I can run a lightweight data room — organized shared folders with view-only links, download controls, and access visibility for diligence
As a developer, search reaches inside files — a documented search API over filenames and full-text content, not just prefix matching
As a developer, files carry my schema — custom metadata/properties templates that can be set and queried via the API
As a developer, previews are an API call — thumbnails and embeddable document previews served for common formats without me rendering them
As an operations lead, signatures happen where the files live — a native e-signature product or documented first-party signing integration
As an operations lead, documents are editable in place — real-time co-editing of docs/sheets/slides in the browser, native or via a documented integration
As an AI-native team, the storage understands its contents — a first-party AI surface (ask questions of files, summarize, extract) shipped and documented, not just announced
As an IT admin, the team is manageable by API — member provisioning, group management, and admin endpoints documented for automation
As a security engineer, activity is auditable — team event/audit logs with documented API access or SIEM export
As a founder, storage pricing is published — per-plan storage quotas and per-user prices on a public page, including what happens at the cap
As a power user, I can start free — a real free tier with published storage quota that works with the same clients and API
